source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-13: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 13 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For Variant 13 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition, explain the RDMA data path for multi-node GPU training or inference without asserting unmeasured platform facts. State assumptions and identify hardware, topology, NIC/link, GPU-direct capability, driver, framework, transport, and fallback settings that must be recorded. Trace an operation from the application collective or point-to-point call through the communication library and verbs interface (queue pairs, work requests/completions, registered memory, protection/access permissions) to transport and NIC/link activity, remote memory or GPU buffers, synchronization, and completion; distinguish zero-copy or GPU-direct paths from host staging and explain when fallback can occur. Define a falsifiable hypothesis against a named baseline, with a workload distribution over message sizes, batch/parallelism, ranks, and topology; specify warm-up, steady-state window, repetitions, clock sources, and units. Measure end-to-end and per-operation communication time, overlap and GPU step time, throughput, latency percentiles, CPU utilization, queue/completion errors, retransmissions or link events where available, and relevant device counters, but do not treat a device counter as proof of application improvement. Analyze confounders such as congestion, NUMA/PCIe placement, overlap, caching, power state, software version, and workload mix; report uncertainty and separate measurements from estimates. For the link-failure requirement, define detection and bounded recovery behavior, error classification, timeout/retry limits, health checks, and a safe fallback or rollback trigger that preserves correctness and avoids silent data corruption; state what evidence is required before enabling RDMA or claiming a benefit. Do not expose credentials or sensitive telemetry, and do not promise an SLO without representative measurements.
